Factors like language fluency, cultural context, anxiety, and access to tutoring can dramatically change results. As a result, standardized tests measure how well someone performs on a specific kind of timed academic task, not intelligence itself. Intelligence includes creativity, practical problem-solving, adaptability, social-emotional reasoning, and the capacity to learn in real-world situations, none of which are fully assessed by a multiple-choice exam.
